title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: motives over R, as on the previous page. The data are:
- G = Aut_⊗(T_B), the motivic Galois group for the Betti fibre functor.
- f_∞ ∈ G(Q), the real Frobenius, with f_∞^2 = 1. It is induced by complex conjugation on X(C).
- P = Isom_⊗(T_B⊗R, T_DR), the period torsor. Its class is given by the Z/2-cocycle with value f_∞.
- j : S_R → G_R, the Hodge cocharacter of the Deligne torus, satisfying f_∞ j(λ) f_∞^{-1} = j(λ̄).

Part 1 (top of page). This finishes an argument started on earlier pages, not available here. α, β, γ are points of the period torsors (P, P' and a subtorsor Q). For a point x of a real torsor, R(x) is its residue field, either R or C. Since β is an R-point (β ∈ Q(R) ⊂ P'(R)), adjoining β changes nothing. So R(γ) = R(β,γ) = R(β,α) = R(α). The conclusion is that this residue field is C, except in an 'exceptional case' specified earlier. That case is presumably when the relevant torsor is trivial, i.e. f_∞ acts trivially or the Hodge structure is purely real/Tate.

Part 2 (Remark). Let M be a motive over R with Betti realization T_B(M). Claim: (f_∞)_M = id only if M is a sum of tensor powers of Q(2). The underlying reason:
- The de Rham conjugation τ = f_∞σ preserves the Hodge filtration and its conjugate, so τ preserves each H^{p,q}.
- Hence f_∞ = τσ maps H^{p,q} onto H^{q,p}.
- So f_∞ = id forces M to be of pure Hodge–Tate type (p,p).
- Granting a Hodge-conjecture-type statement, M is then a sum of Artin twists A(-p).
- On Q(1) = 2πiQ, f_∞ acts by -1, so the even Tate twists Q(2n) qualify.

Part 3 (largely struck out, then partly resumed). Specialize λ = i in the Hodge relation:
- Let C = j(i) be the Weil operator. Then f_∞ C f_∞^{-1} = j(-i) = C^{-1} = ηC, with η = w(-1) the weight cocharacter at -1.
- So f_∞ lies in the transporter Norm(C, C^{-1}).
- The struck lines invoke K = Cent(C), of index 1 or 2 in K'·Norm, and the fact that K(R) is maximal compact. This is Deligne's principle that int(C) is a Cartan involution, coming from polarizability.

Grothendieck then passes to Ġ = G/w(G_m) = Ker ε / w(μ_2) and the images ḟ_∞, Ċ. There ḟ_∞ ∈ K' := Norm(Ċ, Ċ^{-1}) ⊃ K = Cent(Ċ). The aim is evidently to show that f_∞ lies, modulo weights, in the maximal compact subgroup defined by the Weil operator, i.e. that f_∞ commutes with the Cartan involution. The page breaks off before concluding; the next page turns to Hodge cohomology over abstract topological fields ≅ C.
errors: The Remark as written ('only if M is a sum of tensor powers of Q(2)') is too strong. Let ε be the rank-one Artin motive over R defined by h^0(Spec C) = 1 ⊕ ε; f_∞ acts on ε by -1. Then ε(1) = ε⊗Q(1) also has f_∞ = +1, and ε(1)^{⊗2} = Q(2). The correct statement, assuming Hodge–Tate implies Artin–Tate, is that M is a sum of tensor powers of ε(1). Equivalently, M is a sum of Q(2n) and ε(2n+1)-type pieces: in each Hodge type (p,p), Artin factor trivial for p even and ε for p odd. Unless the archive's 'Q(2)' denotes something else, an Artin twist is missing.

In Ġ = G/w(G_m), η = w(-1) maps to 1, so Ċ^2 = 1 and Ċ^{-1} = Ċ. Hence K' = Norm(Ċ, Ċ^{-1}) is just the centralizer of Ċ, and the inclusion K ⊂ K' is an equality. The distinction drawn (and the struck 'index 1 or 2' remark) is vacuous in Ġ. It only matters in G itself.
Part 1 relies on definitions (α, β, γ, Q, P', 'cas exceptionnel') from earlier pages not provided; it cannot be checked fully here.

ideas.what: Real Frobenius f_∞ as an element of order 2 of the motivic Galois group, with the period torsor's class given by the cocycle f_∞ and the relation f_∞ C f_∞^{-1} = C^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Real Frobenius F_∞ in the motivic/Mumford–Tate group; F_∞ normalizes the Hodge cocharacter (h ∘ conj)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne ('Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales', 1979); Saavedra Rivano (1972); Deligne–Milne (1982)

ideas.what: Residue field of points of period torsors over R equals C except in an exceptional case
ideas.modern_name: Field of definition of period points / nontriviality of the real period torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1979 (periods c±); general torsor formalism Saavedra/Deligne

ideas.what: Motives over R with trivial F_∞ are Hodge–Tate of even weight (up to Artin twists)
ideas.modern_name: F_∞ swaps H^{p,q} and H^{q,p}; F_∞-invariant motives are Artin–Tate

ideas.what: Weil operator C = j(i), centralizer K of C in G/w(G_m) maximal compact; f_∞ in normalizer/centralizer
ideas.modern_name: int(C) is a Cartan involution of the adjoint/weight-quotient group (polarizability); F_∞ commutes with it

missed.claim: Historical priority detail: ca. 1969–72 Grothendieck already set up the real Frobenius in the Tannakian motivic group and tied it to the de Rham real structure via the period torsor and the cocycle f_∞. He also related it to the Weil operator and the maximal compact defined by C. This predates Deligne's 1979 treatment of F_∞ and real periods, though all of it is now standard.
missed.quote: f∞ C f∞^{-1} = C^{-1} = ηC ... Considérons G/i(G_m) = Ġ ... ḟ∞ ∈ Norm_{Ġ_R}(Ċ, Ċ^{-1})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only for attribution/history of the motivic Galois group over R; no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Coherent early sketch of real Frobenius and period torsor over R. It matches what Saavedra and Deligne later published and contains a minor error in the Remark (an Artin twist ε(1) is missing). Nothing absent from the modern literature.
transcription_corrections: 'J_B(M)' should read 'T_B(M)' (Betti fibre functor); the struck word before it is probably 'représentation' rather than 'Grassmann'.
'f_∞ M = id_M' should read '(f_∞)_M = id_M', with subscript M.
In the struck passage, 'f_∞ g(λ) f_∞^{-1} = g(λ^{-1})' should read 'f_∞ j(λ) f_∞^{-1} = j(λ′)' (λ′ the canonical conjugation on S_R), matching the previous page.
'λ = C ∈ S(R' should read 'λ = C ∈ S(R)', i.e. the element i ∈ S(R) = C^*, giving C = j(i).
'qui est donc = C [?]' is 'qui est donc = C' (complex numbers); there is a blank before '=' in the original.
'[= Ker ε / i(μ_2)]': the original appears to read 'Ker ε / i(μ_2)' (or i(H_2)); i is the weight cocharacter.
